---
title: "Repository layout"
---


```
_extensions/easyqda-theme/   the format: _extension.yml, easyqda.scss
                            (all rules), easyqda-light/-dark.scss
                            (palettes only)
font/                       Noto Sans woff2 subsets + noto.css (SIL OFL 1.1)
offline/postprocess.py      the three offline repairs, loud on drift
offline/smoketest.py        the headless-browser proof
offline/mathjax/            vendored MathJax (Apache 2.0)
print/                      the one-PDF builder and the Noto TTFs it embeds
script/gen_versions.py     maintains versions.json from _extension.yml
example/minimal/            the site the CI renders and smokes
example/site-publish.yml    template for a site's publish workflow
doc/                        this documentation (en/ + de/), built with
                            the theme itself
doc-root/                  the language chooser and the bare-address
                            shortcut this site deploys
```

## How consumers use it

The zotQDA sites **vendor** the theme rather than fetching it at build
time: qdaPy and qdaR each keep the single copy in `docs/_theme/`
(mirrored into the language projects by their `build.sh`), plus
`offline/` and `print/` beside it, and each carries an
`update-theme.sh` that re-copies everything from a sibling checkout of
this repository. Change the theme here, run `update-theme.sh` there,
rebuild, commit — the sites build in CI without this repository
existing.

This documentation is the exception that proves the layout: it lives
*inside* the theme repository, so its `doc/build.sh` mirrors
`_extensions/` and `font/` straight from the repository root — the
one copy with no vendoring step at all.

## The example as a contract

`example/minimal/` is deliberately tiny — a `_quarto.yml` and one
page. The CI renders it with the pinned Quarto, applies the offline
repairs and runs the smoketest on every push. Anything the theme
promises should be observable there; anything that breaks should
break there first, not in a consumer's build.
